nodes.summary: A Frobenius congruence restricts along a compatible pair: if `ι : C →ₐ[R] B` and `ρ : G →* H` satisfy `ι (ρ g • c) = g • ι c`, and `σ` is a Frobenius at `Q`, then `ρ σ` is a Frobenius at `Q.comap ι`.
nodes.title: Restriction of a Frobenius element along a compatible pair

nodes.summary: If `σ` is a Frobenius at `Q` and `τ` satisfies the Frobenius congruence at `Q.comap ι`, then `ρ σ = τ` when the inertia subgroup of `Q.comap ι` is trivial. This is the equality form of the restriction statement of Proposition 7.22 under its unramified hypothesis.
nodes.title: Restriction of Frobenius equals Frobenius with trivial inertia

nodes.summary: Two elements satisfying the same powered congruence differ by an element of the inertia subgroup of `Q`.
nodes.title: Elements with the same powered congruence differ by inertia

nodes.summary: In a finite ring tower `R → T → B`, the intermediate prime residue quotient has cardinality equal to the base residue cardinality raised to its canonical inertia degree. The cardinality theorem is Mathlib's `cardQuot_pow_inertiaDeg`.
nodes.title: Intermediate residue cardinality as a power of the base residue cardinality

nodes.summary: Powers of an arithmetic Frobenius map satisfy the powered congruence: if `φ x - x ^ q ∈ Q` for all `x`, then `(φ ^ f) x - x ^ q ^ f ∈ Q`.
nodes.title: Powers of a Frobenius map satisfy the powered congruence

nodes.summary: If `σ` is a Frobenius at `Q` and `τ` satisfies the powered congruence with exponent `q ^ f`, then `σ ^ f = τ` when the inertia subgroup of `Q` is trivial. This is a uniqueness helper for an already supplied powered congruence. The actual tower theorem below derives that congruence from the Frobenius premise over the intermediate ring and its residue cardinality.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of Frobenius powers with trivial inertia

nodes.summary: Powers of an arithmetic Frobenius element satisfy the powered congruence: if `σ • x - x ^ q ∈ Q` for all `x`, with `q = Nat.card (R ⧸ Q.under R)`, then `(σ ^ f) • x - x ^ q ^ f ∈ Q`.
nodes.title: Powers of a Frobenius element satisfy the powered congruence

nodes.summary: For algebra automorphisms in a finite ring tower, the inclusion of the intermediate Frobenius is the canonical `AlgEquiv.restrictScalars`.
nodes.title: Frobenius tower equality for algebra automorphisms

nodes.summary: The tower equality for the source's intermediate field `E ⊂ L`. Here `K` is the fraction field of the base ring `R`, `T` is the integral closure of `R` in `E`, and `B` is its integral closure in `L`. In the number-field application these are the three rings of integers. The intermediate action is `E.fixingSubgroup`; the whole `Gal(L/K)` need not fix `T`.
nodes.title: Frobenius tower equality for an intermediate field

nodes.summary: In a finite ring tower `R → T → B`, the Frobenius over `T`, embedded into an action over `R`, equals the Frobenius over `R` raised to the intermediate residue degree when the inertia subgroup is trivial. Only `H` must fix `T`.
nodes.title: Frobenius in a tower is a power of the base Frobenius
